# Incident Report: 2024-09-04 Traffic Analysis Exercise

## Victim Host
| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 address | 172.17.0.99 |
| MAC address | 18:3d:a2:b6:8d:c4 |
| Windows hostname | DESKTOP-RNVO9AT (workgroup/domain NetBIOS name: BEPOSITIVE, AD domain: bepositive.com, DC: WIN-CTL9XBQ9Y19) |
| Logged-in Windows user | afletcher (confirmed via Kerberos AS/TGS exchanges with cname `afletcher`, realm BEPOSITIVE.COM, between 172.17.0.99 and DC 172.17.0.17) |

## Malware Family
**Koi Stealer** — attribution is **signature-confirmed**, not just behavioral. The IDS alerts include an ET Pro rule that names the family directly:

- `ETPRO TROJAN Win32/Koi Stealer CnC Checkin (POST) M2` — fired 48 times, 172.17.0.99 → 79.124.78.197:80, POST /foots.php
- Corroborating generic rule: `ET INFO GENERIC SUSPICIOUS POST to Dotted Quad with Fake Browser 1` (POSTs to a raw IP with a spoofed legacy IE user-agent, a known Koi Stealer beacon trait)

Traffic behavior matches the signature: repeated `POST /foots.php HTTP/1.1` requests (roughly every 70–90 seconds, first at 2024-09-04 17:35:07 UTC, continuing for the remainder of the capture), each with `Content-Type: application/octet-stream`, `Content-Encoding: binary`, and an encrypted/opaque body (40–112 bytes) — consistent with an encrypted stealer check-in rather than real HTTP content. The server (`nginx`) replies `200 OK` with an empty chunked body each time, typical of a beacon acknowledgment.

## Indicators of Compromise

**Command-and-control:**
- `79.124.78.197:80` — primary C2, confirmed by ET Pro Koi Stealer signature. Endpoints hit on this host:
  - `POST /foots.php` (beacon/check-in, repeated ~48 times over the capture)
  - `GET /index.php?id=&subid=qIOuKk7U` — response body: `HckDcK0czXjaq48jVHNn|qIOuKk7U|http://79.124.78.197/index.php|` (affiliate/loader-style tracking token)
  - `POST /index.php` — response was binary/encrypted data (non-printable), likely a secondary encrypted payload or config pulled from the C2
- User-Agent used on all C2 traffic: `Mozilla/4.0 (compatible; MSIE 7.0; Windows NT 10.0; WOW64; Trident/7.0; .NET4.0C; .NET4.0E; .NET CLR 2.0.50727; .NET CLR 3.0.30729; .NET CLR 3.5.30729)` — a spoofed legacy IE string, not a real browser.
- No DNS resolution was seen for `79.124.78.197` — the malware contacts it by hardcoded IP.

**Suspicious precursor connection (likely delivery/staging channel):**
- TLS session to `46.254.34.201:443` with SNI `www.bellantonicioccolato.it`, starting at 17:35:04 UTC — three seconds before the first Koi Stealer beacon. This is the largest single conversation in the capture (~719 KB). Content could not be inspected (no decryption keys available in the evidence), and no DNS query for this hostname was captured, but the timing directly precedes C2 activity and is flagged as the probable infection/staging vector.

**Malicious/suspicious domain:**
- `www.bellantonicioccolato.it` (TLS SNI to 46.254.34.201) — anomalous for this host; unrelated to the legitimate Microsoft/Office/Adobe telemetry domains seen elsewhere in the capture.

**Suspicious request masquerading as legitimate vendor traffic:**
- `GET http://acroipm2.adobe.com/assets/Owner/arm/ProcessMAU.txt` (via Akamai IP 23.220.251.47), sent with the same spoofed IE user-agent used for the confirmed C2 traffic. Response body was only 4 bytes (`****`). This does not match genuine Adobe update-check behavior and is treated as attacker/malware-generated traffic riding on a trusted-looking domain, though it is not independently signature-confirmed.

**Transferred files / hashes:**
- No executable, DLL, or archive payload was observed in cleartext within this capture, and no file names or SHA256 hashes could be extracted. All C2 request/response bodies to 79.124.78.197 were opaque encrypted/binary blobs (`application/octet-stream`), and the only other large-volume exchange (to 46.254.34.201) was TLS-encrypted with no keys available. If an initial dropper/executable was retrieved, it happened either before this capture began or inside the encrypted TLS session to `www.bellantonicioccolato.it`.

## Noted but assessed as non-indicative (false-positive-prone internal alerts)
The alert log also contains several `GPL NETBIOS SMB` / `RPC Kerberos` alerts (SMBv1 use, NTLMSSP overflow signature, IPC$ access, Kerberos principal overflow signature) strictly between 172.17.0.99 and the internal DC 172.17.0.17 on ports 139/88. These correspond to normal domain-joined SMB/Kerberos authentication traffic (afletcher's workstation talking to WIN-CTL9XBQ9Y19) and are legacy GPL rules known for high false-positive rates on legitimate AD traffic. No exploit payload or lateral-movement artifact was found in this traffic; not counted as compromise indicators.

## Summary
User **afletcher** on workstation **DESKTOP-RNVO9AT** (172.17.0.99, MAC 18:3d:a2:b6:8d:c4) was infected with **Koi Stealer** (signature-confirmed via ET Pro rule). Infection activity begins at **2024-09-04 17:35:04–17:35:07 UTC** with a TLS connection to `www.bellantonicioccolato.it` (46.254.34.201) immediately followed by persistent encrypted beaconing to C2 **79.124.78.197:80** (`/foots.php`, `/index.php`), which continued every 70–90 seconds through the end of the capture (~1 hour). No plaintext payload file or hash was recoverable from this traffic alone.
